Fixed. Here's what was happening and what I changed.

## Root cause

`entire repo mirror create` registers the mirror, then polls the cluster's smart-HTTP `info/refs` endpoint every 2s until it advertises a resolvable `HEAD`, printing a dot each tick. The bug was in that polling client.

The cluster front door (`aws-us-east-2.entire.io`) doesn't serve `info/refs` directly — it responds with an **HTTP 307 redirect** to the node actually holding the mirror (`bishop.aws-us-east-2.entire.io`), with a pull token embedded in the redirect URL's userinfo. `git clone` follows that redirect, which is exactly why cloning works.

But the probe's HTTP client was deliberately configured **not** to follow redirects:

```go
CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error {
    return http.ErrUseLastResponse
},
```

So every probe saw the 307, `mirrorAdvertisesHead` treated "not 200" as "not ready," the wait loop fell into its `default` branch, and it printed a dot — forever, regardless of whether the clone had finished. The original code comment assumed any redirect meant misconfiguration (a login page); in reality the cluster uses 307s for node routing.

I reproduced it deterministically: the real loop logged `status=307` on every tick, while a plain `http.DefaultClient` (which follows redirects) fetched the full ref advertisement and resolved `HEAD` to `refs/heads/main` in one shot.

`cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror_probe.go` — the probe now follows redirects, confined to the original cluster host or a subdomain of it, over HTTPS, with a hop cap (`checkProbeRedirect`). The host confinement matters because the redirect carries the pull token in its userinfo — following it to an arbitrary host would leak the token. A stray redirect to a login page still can't cause a false "ready," because readiness is gated on the body decoding as a git advertisement with a resolvable `HEAD`, not on the status code.

Verified against the live mirror — it now prints `ready to use` immediately instead of spinning dots.

In `repo_mirror_test.go`:

Confirmed — your memory is right. This is a **client-side regression introduced Monday**, not a server change.

## Timeline

| When | Commit | Probe HTTP client | Behavior |
|------|--------|-------------------|----------|
| Sat 2026-05-30 | `63866e2b3` "Wire entire repo mirror" | `http.DefaultClient` | ✅ works |
| **Sun 2026-05-31** | *(no changes)* | `http.DefaultClient` | ✅ **works — what you remember** |
| Mon 2026-06-01 16:10 | `c18e10df0` "drop http.DefaultClient, cap the body read" | purpose-built `probeClient` with `CheckRedirect → http.ErrUseLastResponse` | ❌ dots never stop |

## What broke it

The original probe (Sat) used `http.DefaultClient.Do(req)`. `http.DefaultClient` **follows redirects by default** (up to 10 hops), so when the cluster front door 307-redirected `info/refs` to the backing node (`bishop.<cluster-host>`), the probe silently followed it and saw the real advertisement. That's why it worked Sunday.

Monday's commit `c18e10df0` (by Paulo, Claude Opus 4.7-assisted) swapped `http.DefaultClient` for a hardened `probeClient` and, as part of that, added:

```go
// info/refs is a single GET; a redirect would indicate misconfiguration
// (e.g. cluster host fronted by something that 30x's to a login page).
// Surface it as an error rather than silently following.
CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error {
    return http.ErrUseLastResponse
},
```

The commit's other goals were all sound (own client, explicit timeouts, capped body read). The one detail that broke it was the redirect policy — built on the assumption *"info/refs should never redirect."* That assumption was wrong: **the cluster front door has been 307-redirecting to the node all along.** `DefaultClient` had been masking it by following silently; the moment the client was told to refuse redirects, readiness detection died.

## Why it slipped through

- The 307 behavior is server-side and invisible unless you inspect the raw response — the commit author had no reason to suspect `info/refs` redirected.
- It's a *background* probe; nothing fails loudly. The mirror still works (`git clone` follows the redirect itself), so the only symptom is cosmetic-looking dots that never terminate — easy to miss in review and not covered by a test.

My fix (PR #1327) restores redirect-following but more safely than the original blanket `DefaultClient`: it keeps the hardened client and only follows redirects confined to the cluster trust domain via `discovery.HostInCluster`, with the regression test that was missing. So we keep Monday's robustness improvements and undo just the part that broke it.
